Build, test & document components 

 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
Storybook is a frontend workshop for building UI components and pages in isolation. Thousands of teams use it for UI development, testing, and documentation. Find out more at storybook.js.org !

 Examples

View the Storybook Showcase to see how leading teams use Storybook.

Use storybook.new to quickly create an example project in Stackblitz.

 AI

Storybook makes building UI with agents faster, better and cheaper. Your agent reuses the components you already have, writes stories for what it builds, tests its work by running stories, and gives you a visual review to check the result.

 Skills and the CLI

Run this command in the root of your project to install Storybook's skills:

 

Skills are short instruction files in your repository that tell your agent what to do at each step of a UI change. Most AI agents support skills. Your agent learns how to interact with Storybook by reading skill files, and then calls the storybook tools command to get work done:

 Command 
 --------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 storybook tools docs list List all components and docs entries 
 storybook tools docs show Show the props and usage examples of a component 
 storybook tools stories changed List the stories that are new, modified, or affected by uncommitted changes 
 storybook tools test run Run story tests, with accessibility checks if set up 
 storybook tools review create Publish a review of the stories that a change affects 

See Connect your agent to get started, and the CLI options for all the tools. If you want your agent to call Storybook through MCP tools instead of CLI commands, the MCP addon serves the same tools from your dev server.

These features are available for React, Next, TanStack, Vue, Angular, Svelte, Web Components and multiple community frameworks. Check the supported frameworks for more details.

 Published Storybooks

When you publish your Storybook with Chromatic, Chromatic also publishes its MCP server, at your published Storybook's URL followed by /mcp :

 

Agents that connect to the MCP server can look up your components, with their props and usage examples, without running Storybook. This lets the teams that build with your design system reuse its components from their own repositories. Chromatic MCP hosting is entirely free. See Use a published Storybook and Chromatic's setup guide for more details.

See the frameworks documentation for requirements and setup instructions.

 Addons

Addons extend Storybook with features for component design, documentation, testing, interactivity, and so on. Add one to your project with npx storybook add .

 Addons Downloads 
 --------------------------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 docs Add high quality documentation to your components 
 a11y Test that your components are accessible 
 links Create links between stories 
 vitest Run your stories as tests in Vitest browser mode 
 visual tests Catch unexpected visual changes in your stories using Chromatic 
 themes Switch your component library themes from the toolbar 
 msw Mock API requests in stories using Mock Service Worker 
 mcp Run a MCP server in your local Storybook 
 designs Embed Figma files and other design previews alongside your story 
 pseudo-states Toggle CSS pseudo states such as :hover and :focus on your components 
 dark-mode Toggle between light and dark mode in Storybook 
 tag-badges Display story tags as badges in the sidebar and toolbar 

Find more in the addon catalog, and see the Addon / Framework Support Table.

Contributions to Storybook are always welcome! 📥 Pull requests and 🌟 Stars and 🕵🏿 Issue reproductions help us out.
